segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: Thanks for making the time — nothing you say gets back to your employer with your name on it. To start, can you walk me through how your work actually gets done day to day?

segments.speaker: subject
segments.text: Mostly it's a mix of the official dashboard and, honestly, a lot of informal information channels — if I need something fast I just ask whoever's closest rather than waiting for the system.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: When the official tools or process get in your way, what do you do instead — any workarounds you've built for yourself?

segments.speaker: subject
segments.text: There's an informal side channel for the weekly numbers. It definitely gets people the information they need faster in a pinch.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: Where do things most often stall or pile up waiting on someone or something?

segments.speaker: subject
segments.text: The official report, when it finally comes out, might have slightly different numbers or a different interpretation than what was shared informally. It can lead to confusion, and I'm doing redundant work, answering the same questions multiple times.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: Was that more about the tools, the process, or a decision someone made? There's no wrong answer — I'm just mapping where the friction sits.

segments.speaker: subject
segments.text: Honestly, it also means that sometimes I'm probably underutilized about a day a week, because a lot of my time is spent waiting for things to clear, or dealing with these ad-hoc requests that arise from the delays.
